inline_text:
Closes #32.

The source ledger says ATLAS technique codes are referenced inline and ASI classification runs throughout, and no code appears in the text. This PR adds a bracketed tag at the end of each clause that describes a behavior the two frameworks cover, for example `[ATLAS AML.T0110, AML.T0051.001; ASI02, ASI04]`, with a one-line legend above the ledger.

- **24 clauses tagged.** The seventeen rows from the issue, plus seven for the sections added on 2026-09-28: Section 3.3 Tool Implementation, the input and output handling list in Section 4, and the lethal trifecta and Rule of Two paragraph.
- **Validation.** Every ATLAS ID was checked against the ATLAS v5.6.0 data file, the current release. Every ASI code was checked against the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026.
- **Three changes from the issue's table.** ATLAS v5.6.0 has AML.T0109 "AI Supply Chain Rug Pull", so the rug pull clause, the runtime invariants clause (hash drift), and the MCP package clause (silent update) carry it.
- **Ledger.** The ATLAS row moves to v5.6.0, and the ATLAS and OWASP rows now point at the inline tags.
- **Not in this PR.** The two Section 4 clauses about an injected agent labeling its own exfiltration as routine are rewritten in #39, so their tags belong there and will follow once #39 settles.

The Last Modified line in deliverables/README.md is also touched by #38 and #39, which is a one-line fix for whichever merges later.

Disclosure: I co-lead the spec workstream of the OWASP Agent Control Standard, and I work at Capsule Security, which runs the hooks.security registry. Neither is cited in this change.

@MatthewKhouzam @flucktemberg-sap this is the PR requested on #32.
